headline: Medium data-leakage and prompt-injection risk from Chatwoot’s broad egress and shared support content; godot_rl_agents is local-only and lowers conflict risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest and emit customer messages and integrates with Slack/Dialogflow/Shopify/Linear, so its outputs may carry attacker-controlled text. godot_rl_agents has no documented input bridge, but if its outputs are manually copied into Chatwoot workflows or support macros, prompt injection becomes plausible. The pairwise path is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is copied into a downstream agent prompt or automation rule
IF godot_rl_agents output is treated as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable any copy-paste bridge between support text and agent prompts
Add a fixed delimiter/template before pasting content
Review one recent Chatwoot automation for instruction-like parsing
Restrict Chatwoot macros to approved placeholders
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, and has broad network egress. godot_rl_agents shows no data classes touched and no egress, so the main leakage path is Chatwoot exporting sensitive support data to external services. Because the pair interaction is indirect and not documented, medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF Chatwoot routes customer messages to a third-party integration
IF support data is included in any outbound API payload
mitigations: Audit enabled Chatwoot integrations
Turn off unused outbound integrations
Mask customer identifiers in test conversations
Check one outbound request log for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress, while godot_rl_agents is documented as network-none and has no write or OAuth scopes listed. There is no shared mutable resource or overlapping write surface in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is not evidenced. The pair appears mostly disjoint, with only a small risk if an external orchestrator couples them.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same resource
IF a shared filesystem or database is added outside the profiles
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate service accounts
Do not mount a shared writable directory
Verify no shared OAuth app is configured
Review one deployment manifest for overlapping writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can produce support reports and messages that another system might consume, but godot_rl_agents has no documented downstream action-taking authority or input parser. Without evidence that B treats A’s output as authoritative, the cascade is limited. Uncertainty remains because the interaction is undocumented, so the safer low severity is appropriate.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents is wired to consume Chatwoot outputs as training or control input
IF a downstream automation acts on Chatwoot-generated text without verification
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Chatwoot outputs
Log one end-to-end sample and inspect for unchecked propagation
Separate support summaries from control inputs
Add a validation step before any downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly handles customer data and messages, while godot_rl_agents shows no data classes touched and no residency or retention constraints. The pairwise compliance issue is therefore mostly one-sided: Chatwoot may need policy controls, but B does not add a documented compliance burden. Because no mismatch is evidenced, only a low residual risk is assigned.
conditions: IF Chatwoot stores regulated customer data in a region or retention policy not approved by the operator
IF support transcripts are exported to a service with stricter residency rules
mitigations: Confirm Chatwoot retention settings
Check whether regulated data is stored in Chatwoot
Disable exports for sensitive tickets
Review one privacy notice against current deployment
